title: 10 Best Simple Ticketing Systems for IT & Support Teams (2027)
summary: Compare 10 simple ticketing systems for IT and support teams in 2027, including key features, ease of use, and pricing.
body_markdown:
Simple ticketing systems have become essential for internal teams that need structure without complexity. Whether you manage IT requests, HR inquiries, or cross-functional employee support, the right ticketing platform turns scattered messages into organized, trackable work.


The challenge is finding a system that adds structure without adding friction. Teams already communicate in Slack, Microsoft Teams, and email. Forcing employees to learn a separate portal or submit requests through unfamiliar interfaces creates barriers that slow response times and frustrate everyone involved. A[Slack-native help desk](https://unthread.io/products/slack-support?ref=unthread.io) keeps the employee experience conversational while giving internal teams the operational controls they need.


## **Key Takeaways**


- Simple ticketing systems prioritize ease of use, fast setup, and minimal context-switching for both requesters and support staff.
- [Unthread](https://unthread.io/?ref=unthread.io) is the recommended option for teams that want Slack-native intake, purpose-built AI agents for triage and resolution, and a self-learning knowledge base that reduces repetitive work.
- Enterprise teams should consider platforms that scale with complex routing, compliance requirements, and multi-department workflows.
- The best ticketing systems let simple questions stay easy to submit while moving sensitive or complex requests into structured workflows.
- Teams should evaluate systems based on their primary communication channels, internal support requirements, privacy needs, and automation capabilities.


## **What Makes a Ticketing System Simple?**


Simplicity in ticketing is not about having fewer features. It is about reducing the effort required to submit, route, track, and resolve requests. A truly simple ticketing system fits into existing workflows rather than demanding new habits.


A strong simple ticketing tool should help teams:


- Convert messages from Slack, email, and chat into tickets automatically
- Route requests by topic, urgency, or requester context
- Keep sensitive matters private when needed
- Automate recurring Tier 1 questions with[knowledge base](https://unthread.io/products/knowledge-base?ref=unthread.io) references
- Track SLAs and ownership without manual updates
- Connect with HRIS, CRM, ITSM, and identity tools through relevant[integrations](https://unthread.io/products/integrations?ref=unthread.io)


The most practical systems keep everyday request intake straightforward while adding structure behind the scenes.


## **1) Unthread: Best AI-Native Internal Help Desk for Slack Teams**


[Unthread](https://unthread.io/?ref=unthread.io) turns Slack, Microsoft Teams, employee portals, and email into a structured internal help desk for IT, HR, finance, procurement, legal, and workplace operations teams. It is built for internal teams that need privacy, routing, ticket ownership, reporting, and automation without forcing employees into a separate help desk portal.


### **Why It Fits Internal Teams**


Unthread is designed for internal support workflows where employees ask questions about IT access, payroll, benefits, leave, policies, onboarding, and equipment. A channel such as #it-help or #hr-help becomes a full internal help desk. General questions can stay in-channel when appropriate, while sensitive matters move into private workflows for confidentiality.


### **Key Capabilities**


- [Purpose-built AI agents](https://unthread.io/products/agentic-ai?ref=unthread.io) for triage, routing, and resolution support
- [Private ticketing](https://unthread.io/solutions/hr-service-desk?ref=unthread.io) for handling sensitive HR requests like payroll, benefits, and employee documents
- [Automations](https://unthread.io/products/automations?ref=unthread.io) for recurring Tier 1 requests, approvals, escalations, and follow-ups
- Self-learning[knowledge management](https://unthread.io/products/knowledge-base?ref=unthread.io) that turns repeated questions into reusable documentation
- [AI analytics](https://unthread.io/products/analytics?ref=unthread.io) for identifying request trends, bottlenecks, and automation opportunities
- [SOC 2 Type II compliance](https://unthread.io/security?ref=unthread.io) and security controls for internal support teams


At Lemonade, Unthread's purpose-built AI agents automatically resolve approximately[40% of incoming tickets](https://unthread.io/blog/case-study-how-lemonade-boosts-efficiency-with-unthread-and-gen-ai/) across multiple internal teams, demonstrating the platform's ability to automate routine employee support requests.


### **What Teams Should Consider**


Unthread is the clearest fit when Slack is already a primary employee workspace and internal teams want to reduce manual triage without adding another place for employees to check. Teams can evaluate Unthread through a[14-day free trial](https://unthread.io/pricing?ref=unthread.io) . The platform offers per-agent pricing, with advanced AI automation and enterprise capabilities available across higher-tier plans.


## **2) Zendesk**


Zendesk is a customer service platform with omnichannel ticketing across email, chat, social, and voice. It offers extensive automation with AI agents included in most plans.


### **Where It Fits**


Zendesk is often evaluated when organizations need a broad service platform that can handle high ticket volumes across multiple channels. It works for both customer support and internal help desk use cases.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Omnichannel ticketing with email, chat, social, and voice support
- AI-assisted ticket routing and automation
- Extensive app integrations via marketplace
- Enterprise-grade scalability with HIPAA compliance options
- Comprehensive reporting and analytics


### **What Teams Should Review**


Teams should review whether Zendesk's broad customer support focus fits internal employee service delivery, and whether Slack-first teams will spend most of their day in a separate interface.


## **3) Freshdesk**


Freshdesk is Freshworks' customer support platform, offering AI automation through Freddy AI for ticket classification and response suggestions. It provides a balance of features and affordability.


### **Where It Fits**


Freshdesk is relevant for teams that want omnichannel support with strong automation at mid-tier pricing. It can support internal service desk workflows, though it is more customer-support oriented.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Freddy AI for automated responses and ticket classification
- Omnichannel support across email, phone, chat, and social
- Built-in gamification for agent motivation
- Workflow automation and SLA management
- Knowledge base and self-service options


### **What Teams Should Review**


Teams should evaluate whether the platform handles private internal requests, Slack-native employee intake, and sensitive HR workflows effectively.


## **4) Zoho Desk**


Zoho Desk offers budget-friendly ticketing options. It includes Zia AI for sentiment analysis and predictions, making it accessible for smaller teams.


### **Where It Fits**


Zoho Desk is often considered by organizations with tight budgets that still need structured ticketing, routing, and automation. It integrates well with the broader Zoho ecosystem.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Zia AI assistant for sentiment analysis and predictions
- Work Modes system for agent productivity
- Support in 40+ languages
- Free tier for up to 3 agents
- Strong integration with Zoho ecosystem


### **What Teams Should Review**


Zoho Desk provides ticket management, workflow automation, and integrations with the broader Zoho ecosystem. Teams should check how well Zoho Desk handles Slack-native intake and whether the Zoho ecosystem integration adds value for their stack.


## **5) Help Scout**


Help Scout takes a human-centered approach by eliminating ticket numbers entirely. The shared inbox looks and feels like email, reducing the learning curve for teams transitioning from scattered inboxes.


### **Where It Fits**


Help Scout is relevant for teams that primarily handle requests via email and want a clean, conversational interface without traditional ticketing complexity.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Shared inbox without ticket numbers
- Built-in knowledge base (Docs) and live chat (Beacon)
- AI-generated drafts and conversation summarization
- Unlimited users on all paid plans
- Clean, email-like interface


### **What Teams Should Review**


Help Scout offers shared inboxes, knowledge management, and AI-assisted responses for teams that prioritize email-based support.


## **6) Jira Service Management**


Jira Service Management, paired with Atlassian Assist, supports conversational ticketing for teams already using Atlassian tools. It offers ITSM capabilities with asset management and ITIL-aligned processes.


### **Where It Fits**


This option is most relevant when internal requests need to connect with Jira Software or when the company already uses Atlassian for IT, operations, and knowledge management.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Native integration with Jira Software and Confluence
- ITSM capabilities with asset management
- Pre-built templates and AI configuration
- Up to 500 automation runs per month on free tier
- Free tier for up to 3 agents


### **What Teams Should Review**


Jira Service Management integrates with Confluence to provide knowledge-based self-service and help employees find answers to common questions. Teams should evaluate whether the Atlassian setup feels natural for non-technical employees.


## **7) LiveAgent**


LiveAgent combines ticketing with built-in call center capabilities for teams that need phone support alongside chat and email.


### **Where It Fits**


LiveAgent is relevant for teams handling requests across multiple channels where phone support is essential.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Built-in call center with phone support
- Multi-channel intake across email, chat, and social
- Extensive integrations
- Ticketing with routing and SLA management
- Real-time chat widget


### **What Teams Should Review**


Teams focused on Slack-native workflows should check whether phone-centric features align with their primary intake channels.


## **8) Hiver**


Hiver operates directly within Gmail, converting shared inboxes into structured help desks without requiring users to leave their email client.


### **Where It Fits**


Hiver is designed for teams that run their operations through Google Workspace and want to manage requests without switching applications.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Gmail-native ticketing within existing interface
- AI features for response suggestions
- Shared inbox collaboration
- SLA tracking and analytics
- G Suite integration


### **What Teams Should Review**


Teams should evaluate whether Gmail-first workflows fit their communication patterns or whether Slack-native intake would better serve their employee experience.


## **9) Intercom**


Intercom offers real-time chat and AI agents (Fin) for automated responses. It is designed for teams that prioritize live conversation over traditional ticketing.


### **Where It Fits**


Intercom is relevant for teams handling high volumes of real-time inquiries where immediate response matters more than structured case management.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Chat-first interface with AI agents (Fin)
- Proactive messaging and automation
- Extensive integrations
- Customer data platform integration
- In-app messaging support


### **What Teams Should Review**


Teams should review whether chat-first support fits internal employee workflows or whether conversational Slack ticketing provides better coverage.


## **10) monday service**


monday service connects ticketing with monday.com's visual project management boards, enabling workflows where support requests link directly to operational work.


### **Where It Fits**


monday service is relevant for teams that already use monday.com for project management and want support requests to flow into the same visual workspace.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Visual workflow boards for ticket management
- Integration with monday.com project management
- Customizable request forms
- SLA tracking and automation
- Team collaboration features


### **What Teams Should Review**


Teams should evaluate whether the visual board approach fits their support operations or whether dedicated ticketing provides cleaner workflows.


## **Why Choose Unthread for Simple Ticketing?**


Internal teams need more than a place to collect requests. They need a system that keeps employee support private, organized, fast, and easy to manage across departments.


[Unthread](https://unthread.io/?ref=unthread.io) fits that need because it combines Slack-native intake with structured ticketing, private workflows, knowledge management, AI analytics, and[automations](https://unthread.io/products/automations?ref=unthread.io) . Employees can keep asking questions in Slack, while internal teams gain the operational control needed to manage every request from intake to resolution.


Unthread is especially useful for teams that want to:


- Turn #it-help or #hr-help into a structured support queue
- Protect sensitive employee issues with[private ticketing](https://unthread.io/solutions/employee-support?ref=unthread.io)
- Use[purpose-built AI agents](https://unthread.io/products/agentic-ai?ref=unthread.io) for triage and automated resolution
- Build a self-learning[knowledge base](https://unthread.io/products/knowledge-base?ref=unthread.io) from resolved tickets
- Track repeat request types and service trends through[AI analytics](https://unthread.io/products/analytics?ref=unthread.io)
- Coordinate work across IT, HR, finance, procurement, legal, and workplace operations


For teams choosing a simple ticketing system in 2027, Unthread is the recommended option when the goal is to modernize internal support without making employees leave the place where they already work.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How does conversational AI improve ticket resolution times?**


Conversational AI reduces resolution times by automatically answering routine questions, routing complex requests to the right team members, and drafting responses based on knowledge base content. Unthread's purpose-built AI agents automate routine employee support requests, including answering questions and routing tickets. At Lemonade, the platform automatically resolves approximately[40% of incoming tickets](https://unthread.io/blog/case-study-how-lemonade-boosts-efficiency-with-unthread-and-gen-ai/) across multiple internal teams. This frees internal teams to focus on higher-value work while maintaining fast response times for employees.


### **Can a simple ticketing system integrate with my existing CRM or project management tools?**


Yes, most modern ticketing systems offer integrations with common business tools. Unthread offers[integrations with enterprise platforms](https://unthread.io/products/integrations?ref=unthread.io) , including Jira, Salesforce, HubSpot, and ServiceNow, allowing teams to maintain connected workflows without manual data entry. These integrations enable automatic data sync, bidirectional updates, and unified reporting across systems. Teams can evaluate integration capabilities during trial periods to ensure compatibility with their existing technology stack.


### **What are the benefits of a self-learning knowledge base?**


A self-learning knowledge base automatically identifies repeated questions from ticket history and generates draft articles for team review. This reduces manual documentation effort while ensuring knowledge stays current.[Unthread's knowledge base](https://unthread.io/products/knowledge-base?ref=unthread.io) also flags outdated content when ticket patterns indicate information gaps. The system learns from resolution patterns to suggest improvements and surface the most helpful content to employees before they submit tickets.


### **Is a Slack-native ticketing system secure for enterprise use?**


Yes, platforms like Unthread maintain[SOC 2 Type II compliance](https://unthread.io/security?ref=unthread.io) , support SSO and SCIM provisioning, and offer HIPAA compliance with Business Associate Agreements on enterprise plans. Slack Enterprise Grid support ensures the platform meets the security requirements of large organizations. These systems provide audit trails, role-based access controls, and data encryption to protect sensitive employee information. Enterprise security features enable internal teams to handle confidential HR, legal, and financial requests within Slack without compromising compliance.
